# Compatible translated fibers and the mass of a rigid deepest stratum

This note isolates a consequence of whole-fiber translation rigidity. It
does not prove that the rigid stratum exhausts the original family.

## 1. The center graph of compatible translates is an actual convex graph

Let P be a finite nonempty subset of Z^n with
P=conv(P) intersect Z^n. Let K be a full-dimensional convex body in R^d,
d>=1, and suppose the prescribed fibers K_p=c_p+K satisfy every integer-
anchored inclusion:

    sum_i lambda_i K_(p_i) subset K_p
    whenever lambda_i>=0, sum_i lambda_i=1,
    sum_i lambda_i p_i=p in P.

Then necessarily

    c_p=sum_i lambda_i c_(p_i).                         (1)

Indeed the inclusion is K+sum lambda_i c_(p_i) subset K+c_p. A nonzero
translation cannot put a compact convex body inside itself: applying
its support function in the displacement direction contradicts such
an inclusion. This proves (1), without assuming a global affine formula
for c_p between integer bases.

Put T={(p,c_p):p in P}, G=conv(T). Equation(1) says exactly that

    G intersect (Z^n times R^d)=T.                     (2)

In particular every convex subset A of G has at most one point over an
integer base, namely its prescribed center c_p. Thus, for any finite
family of convex subsets A_i of G,

    intersection_i A_i intersects T
      iff intersection_i proj_base(A_i) intersects Z^n. (3)

For the reverse implication, an integer base in every projection lies
in P, and each corresponding fiber point is forced to equal c_p.
There is no assertion about fibers at noninteger bases.

## 2. Existing weighted graph-center input

Give the bases positive weights w_p and put W=sum_p w_p. Equation(1) makes the singleton graph T closed under every admissible same-parity midpoint. Accepted fact bee3cc8e50a0dcea therefore supplies one t in T with weight at least W/2^n in every containing closed ambient halfspace. The case n=0 is a singleton directly. This is reused background.

## 3. Existing unweighted case and an external-density consequence

For equal-volume compatible translates, accepted fact e4253a0d6f78849c gives the unweighted bound Gamma_d |P| |K|/2^n. This is background rather than a new equal-volume theorem.

For the auxiliary externally weighted measure, let g be the centroid of K and V=|K|, assign density w_p/V on c_p+K, and select t=(p,c_p) by Section2. Put y=(p,c_p+g). Every containing cap with continuous normal u includes the translate of the through-g ordinary cap in each fiber whose graph point has nonnegative affine margin. Those graph points have total weight at least W/2^n; ordinary Grunbaum gives at least Gamma_d times that weight. Pure-base caps include the whole selected fibers. Thus the auxiliary density-weighted bound is Gamma_d W/2^n. This is not a change of the target mixed-integer measure.

## 4. Application to an exactly rigid deepest subfamily

Suppose an original compatible family has maximum raw mixed depth Q,
and J is a nonempty subset of its integer bases with all of the
following PROVED properties:

* J is lattice-complete in its convex hull;
* its actual whole fibers are translates of one common K;
* their anchored relations have the equality(1).

The center constructed for this subfamily is an original mixed point,
and each original cap contains at least its subfamily cap mass. Hence

    Q>=Gamma_d (sum_(p in J)|K_p|)/2^n.              (6)

This applies to translation classes only after their closure premises
have been established by the T-then-E rigidity theorem. Formula(6)
does not exhaust mass outside J. In particular knowing merely that
there are at most2^n such classes does not combine their separately
selected centers into one center for the entire original measure.

The graph reduction explains exactly what the rigidity theorem can
supply when its class already contains the whole family. The missing
step for OC is still to control all other fibers or find a compatible
improving deformation; that step is not hidden in Doignon's theorem.
